einzeiler: Andrew Carnegie's 19th-century struggle with his workers and the violent history of US…
kurzfassung: In the late 19th century, the clash between capital and labor turned intensely violent as industrial titans like Andrew Carnegie transformed the American economy. While Carnegie publicly championed workers and philanthropy, his private business strategy sought aggressive efficiency and lower labor costs. This fundamental tension culminated in severe industrial disputes and a high-stakes standoff between management and unionized steelworkers at the Homestead mill.
stichpunkte: An anarchist named Alexander Berkman shot Carnegie Steel manager Henry Clay Frick in July 1892.
The late 19th century was marked by extreme violence and ideological conflict between owners and workers.
Andrew Carnegie built a massive fortune by scaling steel production and focusing relentlessly on reducing costs.
Carnegie publicly supported unions and philanthropic causes through writings like The Gospel of Wealth, while privately opposing union wage structures.
Factory conditions at steel mills like Homestead were brutal, dangerous, and plagued by fatal accidents.
The 1886 Haymarket Riot in Chicago intensified the national panic over labor unrest and anarchist violence.
Workers at the Homestead plant organized under the Amalgamated Association of Iron and Steel Workers to defend their wages and working hours.
An 1889 labor dispute at Homestead led to a temporary union victory after a lockout and violent confrontations with deputies.

clips.hook: Economic revolutions produce grievances for three main reasons
clips.text: Major economic shifts trigger widespread resentment by disrupting traditional methods, enriching a tiny minority, and stripping ordinary people of their autonomy, often culminating in populist movements and violent backlash.

clips.hook: One guy said he lost 40 pounds when he started the job
clips.text: Workers in steel plants endured extreme heat near giant furnaces and molten metal, causing massive physical exhaustion and severe weight loss from constant sweating.

clips.hook: They had this phrase, propaganda of the deed
clips.text: Radical anarchists believed that high-profile violent acts, such as political assassinations, were necessary catalysts to spark a broader revolution against the government.

clips.hook: They get paid based in part on output
clips.text: Unionized skilled workers at the mill negotiated a compensation structure tied directly to the total volume of steel produced, aligning their earnings with factory productivity.

clips.hook: One of the deputies sort of sizes things up and throws his badge
clips.text: During a tense standoff between armed deputies and angry townspeople, a deputized local quickly realized the danger and abandoned his position by discarding his badge and weapon.

beschreibung:
In the first of two shows about the fight between the richest man and the unions at his Homestead steel plant - we look at why Andrew Carnegie decided that his workforce deserved a smaller share of his profits and the lengths he went to to cut their wages.
Carnegie grew up in poverty and publicly proclaimed that rich moguls such as he had a duty to aid the poor - but that didn't stop him using every weapon at his disposal to crush the steel workers' union. The fight got violent - very violent - and its ripples are still being felt to this day.
